subject.title: Feature request: Hook event for context pruning

question: What pruning-hook contract should OpenClaw support for this issue: metadata-only by default, raw pruned content behind an explicit trusted opt-in, or no core hook yet?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API decides what session/tool metadata or content may leave the context-building path and how hook latency/security boundaries are enforced.

options.title: Metadata-only session prune hook
options.body: Add a session:prune lifecycle event in the active agent-hooks path with bounded counts, timestamp, session identity when available, and sanitized tool metadata only.

options.title: Trusted raw-content opt-in
options.body: Expose pruned content only behind explicit trusted plugin or hook permission with privacy, size, timeout, and logging rules.

options.title: Defer core hook surface
options.body: Keep scheduled indexing as the workaround until a broader memory or hook API design covers pruning, reset, and compaction together.

recommendation.title: Metadata-only session prune hook
recommendation.body: Add a session:prune lifecycle event in the active agent-hooks path with bounded counts, timestamp, session identity when available, and sanitized tool metadata only.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the open implementation candidate and has adjacent hook-surface history.
